title: The Mishra Family Is Back — But the Oldest Son Is Someone New, and Every NRI Who Grew Up Middle-Class Should Care
excerpt: Gullak Season 5 drops June 5 on SonyLIV with Anant Joshi replacing Vaibhav Raj Gupta as Annu. The beloved TVF show about the smallest moments of Indian family life returns at a time when its diaspora audience needs it most.
body:
There's a particular ache that hits when you're 8,000 miles from home and someone sends you a clip from *Gullak*. It's never the dramatic scenes — it's always something painfully specific. Shanti ji haggling over vegetables. Santosh ji reading the newspaper while ignoring a family crisis. Annu making a plan that's equal parts ambition and delusion.

That ache is about to get sharper. The Mishra family is back for a fifth season, arriving June 5 on SonyLIV — and this time, one of its faces has changed.

## A New Annu, the Same Restless Energy

The trailer, which dropped today, confirms what had been rumoured for weeks: **Anant Joshi** has replaced **Vaibhav Raj Gupta** in the role of Anand "Annu" Mishra, the older son who has spent four seasons oscillating between dreams of making it big and the gravitational pull of his modest Bhopal household.

The recasting is significant. Vaibhav's Annu was one of Indian OTT's most relatable characters — a young man whose failures never felt like plot devices, just life happening. Anant Joshi, known for his work in *Kota Factory* and *Panchayat*, steps into shoes that millions of viewers have watched wear down, season by season.

The rest of the core cast returns intact. **Jameel Khan** and **Geetanjali Kulkarni** reprise Santosh and Shanti Mishra — the parents whose marriage is a masterclass in silent communication, passive-aggressive chai-making, and unconditional love disguised as constant complaint. **Harsh Mayar** returns as younger son Aman, and **Sunita Rajwar** is back as the neighbour who knows everyone's business before they do.

## What's New in the Mishra Household

The logline for Season 5 hints at a family navigating upgrades and upheavals. Annu is "battling the familiar pressure of proving himself" — a description that could apply to every eldest son in a middle-class Indian family who's ever been asked, "So what are you doing with your life?"

Aman returns "quieter than before, carrying secrets of his own." And in the show's most delightful new thread, Shanti Mishra has apparently become a minor internet celebrity as "Bittu Ki Mummy" — finding herself, as the show puts it, "in a world suddenly obsessed with being seen."

**Vijay Koshy**, president at TVF, said: *"Season five reflects the changing realities of middle-class India while holding onto the warmth and simplicity that make the show special. This season is about growth, change, and the bittersweet feeling of moving forward while staying connected to your roots."*

Geetanjali Kulkarni added that her character offers "a slightly different side" this season — *"one that's adapting to a rapidly changing world in her own unique way."*

## Why This Show Hits Different When You're Abroad

*Gullak* — the word means piggy bank — has been narrated since Season 1 by the family's old *gullak*, a device that sounds whimsical until you realize it's the show's thesis: that the smallest savings, the tiniest moments, are the ones that matter most.

For the Indian diaspora, this isn't just a show. It's a mirror held up to the life they left behind. The cramped kitchen where your mother cooked miracles. The father who never said "I love you" but showed up at 4 AM to drive you to the train station. The brother you fought with over the last samosa.

**SonyLIV is available internationally** — US, UK, Canada, Australia, the Gulf — so NRIs can watch on day one. If your family group chat hasn't started the countdown yet, give it a week.

## The Question Gullak Keeps Asking

Every season circles back to the same quietly devastating question: *Can you ever really outgrow where you come from?*

For millions of Indians who did leave — who moved to Bangalore or Boston, who traded the *gullak* for a 401(k) — the answer is always the same uncomfortable, comforting truth.

No. And you wouldn't want to.

*Gullak Season 5 premieres June 5, 2026, on SonyLIV. All previous seasons are available for streaming.*
